entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Andrew, Duke of Calabria, a prominent member of the noble House of Árpád, played a pivotal role in the medieval European landscape. Born into the Hungarian royal family, Andrew rose through the ranks to become a key figure in the governance of Calabria, a strategic region in southern Italy. His marriage to Joanna I of Naples, daughter of the Holy Roman Emperor Charles IV, solidified his position as a major player in the complex web of alliances and rivalries that defined the medieval Mediterranean. Through his diplomatic efforts and military campaigns, Andrew contributed significantly to the shaping of Calabrian politics and the fate of the Kingdom of Naples. His legacy continued to influence the region long after his death in 1345, leaving behind a lasting impact on the cultural, economic, and political landscape of the Mediterranean world. As the first husband of Joanna I, Andrew's connection to the Holy Roman Empire underscores the intricate networks of power and influence that characterized the medieval era. His story serves as a testament to the enduring power of family, loyalty, and strategic maneuvering in the pursuit of power and influence.
